title: Age-related change in peak oxygen uptake and change of cardiovascular risk factors. The HUNT Study
authors: Letnes JM, Dalen H, Aspenes ST, Salvesen O, Wisloff U, Nes BM
population: 1,431 healthy adults with directly measured VO2peak in HUNT3 (2006-08) and HUNT4 (2017-19)
findings: Average ten-year decline in VO2peak was non-linear: about 3% in the third decade of life rising to about 20% in the eighth decade, and more pronounced in men.
Linear mixed models with an additional 2,933 HUNT3-only observations showed similar age-related decline.

Self-reported adherence to leisure-time physical activity recommendations was associated with better maintenance of VO2peak, with intensity seemingly more important than minutes of activity at higher age.
One mL/kg/min better VO2peak maintenance was associated with lower odds of hypertension (OR 0.95), dyslipidemia (0.92) and metabolic syndrome (0.86).
limitations: General population, not runners; leisure-time activity self-reported; VO2peak in a mostly untrained sample.
implications: Model the age-related fitness decline as accelerating, not constant: about 3%/decade in the 20s rising to about 20%/decade in the 70s. A planning figure of 5-10%/decade for the 40s-50s is the verifier's/librarian's interpolation, not in the abstract; fit to the runner's own data.
Retain some high-intensity work for older runners: intensity appears more important than total minutes for maintaining VO2peak at higher ages (association, self-reported).
Decline was more pronounced in men here, which differs from Ganse 2020 (no sex difference in annual percentage performance decline); keep sex-neutral defaults.

verification.notes: Crossref and Europe PMC abstract match; all numbers confirmed. The abstract says more pronounced in men, added to limit sex-neutral claims.
